paper.note: Light ground; text on inverted fields. CSS --background (light).

ink.note: Light text, rules, slab, primary button; dark ground. CSS --foreground (light), --background (dark).

snow.note: Dark-theme text, rules and slab field. CSS --foreground (dark).

down.note: Unfavourable move and failure, light theme. CSS --down, --destructive.

slab-up.note: Inside the ink slab on light. CSS --slab-up. Borrows the dark pair.

slab-up-dark.note: Inside the snow slab on dark. CSS --slab-up (dark).

display.purpose: The bank name in the slab only. 1.875rem below 640px, 2.75rem above.

rate.purpose: The slab's whole-number rate. 3.75rem below 640px, 4.5rem above; Rs and decimals beside it at 60% opacity.

headline.purpose: Section heads over a 2px ink rule.

body.purpose: Hints, table text, slab meta, footer copy.

label.purpose: Buttons, segmented controls, status line, footer column heads.

numeral.purpose: Every rate, spread, count and change figure.

code.purpose: Currency codes after a flag; 1.125rem 700 in list rows, 0.875rem 600 in chips.

motion.name: slab-wipe
motion.purpose: The only authored motion: slab figures fade and rise in when currency, bank or side changes. Removed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: hover-fill
motion.value: background-color transition to the wash colour
motion.purpose: Chips, icon buttons, list and table rows.

rules.name: rule-structural

rules.name: rule-on-inverted

narrative.overview:
LKR Rates reads like a bank's own rate board, rebuilt in print: pure white paper, near-black ink, and one answer set solid. The page is organised around a single inverted block, the slab, that names the bank paying the most and its rate at monumental size. Everything else is crisp ruled monochrome: 2px ink rules under the header and every section head, 1px hairlines between rows, and tight 4-6px corners. Depth comes from inversion (ink on paper becomes paper on ink), never from shadow.

The system is dense but calm. Numbers do the talking in JetBrains Mono with tabular, slashed-zero figures so columns align and 0 never reads as O. Poppins carries the bank name and section heads; Inter carries everything a person reads as a sentence. Colour is reserved for movement only, green up and red down, and always travels with an arrow and a sign. Both themes are first-class: the dark theme is the exact inversion of the light one, and the slab inverts with it.

The world explicitly refuses the category default: a soft dark fintech dashboard of rounded cards, green glows and gradient tiles.
keyCharacteristics: One inverted slab per screen carries the answer; nothing else competes with it.
Solid rules (2px ink for structure, 1px hairline for rows) instead of boxes and cards.
Every number in JetBrains Mono, tabular and slashed-zero.
Colour only for movement, always paired with an arrow and a +/- sign.
Selection and "best" are shown by inversion, not by tint.
Flat: no shadows, no gradients, no glows, no glass.

rules.name: The Movement-Only Rule
rules.body: Colour appears only to mark a rate moving, and a broken state. Selection, rank, emphasis and brand are all ink and paper.

rules.name: The Borrowed Pair Rule
rules.body: Inside the slab, movement uses `slab-up`/`slab-down`, the other theme's pair, so green and red keep their contrast on the inverted field.

rules.name: The Inversion Rule
rules.body: "Selected" and "best" are expressed by swapping ink and paper (active chip, active row, best-value chip), never by a tint, outline glow or colour.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number is JetBrains Mono with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums slashed-zero` (applied to every `.font-mono`). No proportional figures anywhere a rate appears, including the share card.

rules.name: The Bank-Is-The-Headline Rule
rules.body: The largest words on the page are a bank's name; the largest figure is that bank's rate. What the figure means ("Highest buying rate · for 1 USD") sits beneath in body text.

rules.name: The Flat Ink Rule
rules.body: If something needs to stand forward, invert it or rule it. Never lift it with a shadow.

dos: Do put the answer in the slab: bank name in Poppins 800, the rate in JetBrains Mono 700, inverted against the page.
Do set every number in JetBrains Mono with tabular, slashed-zero figures.
Do mark selection and "best" by inverting ink and paper, and add an aria-pressed state or a screen-reader label so it is never visual-only.
Do pair every movement colour with an arrow icon and a +/- sign; inside the slab use `slab-up`/`slab-down`.
Do separate sections with a 2px ink rule under the heading and rows with 1px hairlines.
Do put a flag before every currency code, in the same 14 x 21px frame, with an empty frame when no flag exists so rows stay aligned.
Do show provenance next to every figure: which bank, and how fresh.
Do keep the slab wipe as the only authored motion, and honour reduced motion.
donts: Don't use colour as the only signal for up, down, best, selected or broken.
Don't use colour for brand, emphasis or decoration; it belongs to movement and failure only.
Don't use gradients, glows, drop shadows or glass on any page surface.
Don't build card grids or rounded tiles; use ruled rows, ruled tables and the one slab.
Don't wrap the bank name in a sentence or put a label line above it; the headline is the bank name only.
Don't set display type in a system face or numbers in a proportional face.
